Updated assessment incorporating Beige Book insights:
- Policy stance: The FOMC held at 5.25–5.50% and continues QT, emphasizing lags and data dependence.
- Macro: Growth has slowed from Q3; job gains have moderated but remain solid; inflation has eased but is still above target—consistent with a still-restrictive stance.
- Financial conditions and credit: SLOOS shows broad-based tightening in C&I, CRE, and consumer credit, with weaker loan demand and higher spreads/approval thresholds. This reinforces restrictive financial conditions.
- Beige Book (New York District) read-through: Reports easing labor demand (employment demand easing), softer regional activity, and weaker consumer spending; inflationary pressures moderating; housing markets subdued; inventories appear adequate. These signals point to softer real-side momentum and moderating price pressures.
- Implications: Beige Book corroborates SLOOS-driven headwinds to capex, hiring, CRE, and consumer outlays, tilting near-term growth risks further to the downside while supporting continued disinflation. Policy remains cautiously restrictive; risks are skewed to weaker growth even without additional hikes.

Bottom line: The Beige Book adds incremental evidence of softening demand and labor-market cooling beyond the FOMC statement alone, warranting a slightly more negative near-term growth tilt.
